channel.title: The Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (occrp.org)

item.title: Newly Released Epstein Records Detail Financial Ties Linking Billionaire, Art Adviser and Epstein
item.description: Newly released files detail how Jeffrey Epstein managed finances for an art adviser who received $2.5 million from billionaire Leon Black, highlighting complex money flows that concerned accountants but show no criminal wrongdoing.

item.title: Corruption Case Sparks Street Clashes and Political Showdown in Albania
item.description: Demonstrators clash with police while demanding the government resign over charges against the deputy prime minister.

item.title: Slovakia Marks 8 Years Since the Murder of Journalist Ján Kuciak and his Fiancée
item.description: Slovaks are still waiting for justice. A retrial ordered by the Supreme Court of Slovakia is to reveal who masterminded the 2018 assassination.

item.title: Reporter's Notebook: How to Investigate Shadow Fleets
item.description: Tracing a ship's flag is often the first step toward uncovering bigger stories of corruption, smuggling, or sanctions evasion.

item.title: Deadly Raid on Mexican Drug Lord Triggers Unrest in Region Hosting the 2026 World Cup
item.description: After Mexican forces killed Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes, head of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, in a U.S.-backed operation, retaliatory violence spread across several states. An expert speculated the raid was part of preparations for the 2026 World Cup.

item.title: UK to Block Unlicensed Gambling Sponsorship in Sports
item.description: UK to Block Unlicensed Gambling Sponsorship in Sports

item.title: Former Mayor Arrested in Georgia Over Hotel Permit Issued to Wife’s Company
item.description: Georgia arrested a former mayor for allegedly abusing his post when issuing a building permit to the company of his wife. The arrest follows an investigation by OCCRP and iFact that detailed a conflict of interest and construction violations.

item.title: Haitian Police Kill 16 Suspected Gang Members in Anti-Gang Sweep
item.description: Gang violence has displaced over 1.4 million people in Haiti, more than half of whom are children facing extreme forms of exploitation, the UN warned.

item.title: Hungary to Veto New EU Russia Sanctions Over Druzhba Oil Transit
item.description: Hungary says it will block the EU’s planned 20th sanctions package — and other Ukraine-related decisions requiring unanimity — until oil flows to Hungary and Slovakia resume through the Druzhba pipeline, which has been down since late January after reported Russian strikes in western Ukraine.

item.title: Eurojust-Backed Operation Takes Down Ukrainian Scam Call Center
item.description: The Eurojust operation mirrors UN concerns over coerced labor in scam call centers, highlighting the intersection of financial crime and human rights abuses.
